pr_body:
Deeply nested expressions can lead to StackOverflowError at execution planning time.
The parser already has [some protections](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/parser/EsqlParser.java#L81) against this problem, but the optimizers in some cases need more stack frames for the same expressions, so this PR adds similar protections to the rule executors


Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/107752
pr_title: ES|QL: catch StackOverflowError during execution planning
pr_comment: Hi @luigidellaquila, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Oh, that's interesting, it just failed with a StackOverflow. 
More cases to cover apparently
I was a bit reluctant to catch the exception right inside the recursive methods, but there are quite a few places that use them, so it's probably the safest way.

The SO problem seems to reflect on the class loader, that is not good.
Also another (completely unrelated) test in the same suite is failing with the exact same error as a consequence of this, that confirms that the JVM is not in good shape.

Probably we can keep this PR as a first line of defense, but in the long term we could consider a more radical solution, like limiting the allowed depth of expressions at parse time.

review_comment: Should we check that no exception is thrown with the query this "short"?
It could be a test by itself, but I'm not sure it never fails, also at that level. For sure most of the time it succeeds.

I guess this will be test VM-size dependent, so it might require some fiddling if that'll ever be changed. It might be worth leaving a note... though maybe also not, as we have a few tests in similar situation.
Good point, I'll add a comment, it won't hurt

It's completely non-deterministic unfortunately. My feeling is that it also depends on how the JVM JIT inlines some methods, because based on how hot the env is and now many times I run the same test I see a different behavior (ie. sometimes it fails at a certain level, sometimes it needs much deeper expressions, sometimes it never fails)
What is this trying to do? Trigger one of the two types of `ParsingException`s?
See my comment above. Depending on the order of tests, the behavior can change, so the only way to try to catch the StackOverflow at parsing time vs at planning time is to randomize and iterate.
